title: Training Like a Medical Resident: Context-Prior Learning Toward Universal Medical Image Segmentation (Hermes)
mechanism: A universal segmentation model with learned task and modality prior tokens, trained jointly on many heterogeneous, partially labelled datasets.
adaptation: Prior tokens for the 5 BenchmarkEL sources plus UCF-EL. UCF-EL's region-style crack (crack plus inactive) then trains jointly without overwriting the thin-crack convention, and the encoder is not erased because training is joint.
min_experiment: Arm = joint BenchmarkEL + UCF-EL with dataset tokens (3 seeds) versus house PF. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if all gains are < 0.012.
evidence: R: CT/MRI/PET multi-dataset universal segmentation, gains over task-specific and other universal models (abstract level).
prior_overlap: UCF-EL pretrain-then-finetune was n.d. or worse, but the fine-tune erased the encoder. Joint training with dataset priors is open

alt_notes.adaptation: Prior tokens = {5 BenchmarkEL sources, UCF-EL, MultiSolSegment}; an alternative to per-dataset channels for joint EL training.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: prior-token joint training (BenchmarkEL + UCF-EL), 5 seeds vs house PF on BenchmarkEL only; metrics clean-49 crack IoU and E1 relF1@2; kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and test IoU not up by +0.012.
